WebSecureStorageAdapter.getOrCreateEncryptionKey (line ~120) has a race: two concurrent calls can both see no master-key and both generate+store one. The IDB readwrite transaction doesn't prevent this. cachedAdapter singleton init also races if called concurrently from different async contexts.

In openDB(), the db reference returned is used after the Promise resolves, but another concurrent operation could close or delete the database (wipe() calls db.close() then indexedDB.deleteDatabase). A getItem call holding a stale db reference would fail.

No circular dependencies — index.ts imports from secureKeyStorage.ts, no reverse imports
The main file mixes platform detection, crypto utilities, two storage adapters, factory, and high-level API all in one ~400-line file. Adapters and crypto utils should be separate modules.

secureKeyStorage.ts has multiple responsibilities: type definitions, platform detection, crypto helpers, web adapter, RN adapter, factory, and high-level API. Should be split into types.ts, platform.ts, crypto.ts, webAdapter.ts, rnAdapter.ts, index.ts.
Code is generally ESLint-clean; minor: `any` type for keychain in RN adapter would trigger @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any.
Imports are minimal and properly ordered — only internal relative imports.
n/a — no signature verification in this module

AES-GCM IV is generated via crypto.getRandomValues (12 bytes) which is cryptographically random, but there's no explicit uniqueness check before use. If the RNG produced a duplicate IV (astronomically unlikely but possible), the encryption would be compromised. No IV tracking/counter.
n/a — no WebView or iframe content

Critical: Uint8Array from getRandomValues, the encrypted ciphertext, IV, and TextEncoder output are never zeroed after use. The seed hex string persists in memory. No explicit memory wiping (fill(0) on arrays) after operations complete. Sensitive data lingers in GC-managed memory.

RN adapter calls require('react-native-keychain') which is a native module. If an OTA update ships JS that references a native module not in the current binary, it crashes. The try/catch fallback to expo-secure-store helps, but the error handling path itself calls require('expo-secure-store') which could also be missing.

No binary fingerprint or version check before calling native APIs. The code assumes react-native-keychain or expo-secure-store is available without checking the native binary version. An OTA update could ship code that calls APIs not present in older binaries.
Errors are generally propagated via throw with SecureStorageError wrappers. Minor: getTrackedKeys() swallows errors and returns [] instead of propagating.

No distinction between transient and non-transient failures. A failed setItem due to invalid input (non-transient) is treated the same as a transient IndexedDB lock failure. Callers cannot distinguish retryable from non-retryable errors.
n/a — no address handling in this module

RN adapter silently falls back from react-native-keychain to expo-secure-store. This is a storage downgrade — expo-secure-store has different security properties (e.g., no keychain hardware backing on some platforms). The user is not informed of the downgrade. Error is logged but not surfaced.
n/a — no stale armed results pattern
Critical operations throw on failure. Minor: wipe() in RN adapter continues past individual key deletion failures (line ~310) — a failed wipe of a specific key is logged but not fatal.

No deduplication of concurrent operations. Two concurrent setItem('wallet-seed', value1) and setItem('wallet-seed', value2) calls will race — the last one to complete wins, with no ordering guarantee. No mutex/queue on write operations.
n/a — no retry/backoff logic in the module
n/a — no retry logic that could swallow non-transient failures
MockAdapter class in test file is declared but never used in any test case. The SecureStorageAdapter import in the test file is only used as a type for MockAdapter.
No unreachable code — all branches have reachable paths

getTrackedKeys() catch block (line ~330) returns [] instead of propagating — this swallows storage errors. RN adapter wipe() inner catch (line ~310) logs but doesn't propagate individual key wipe failures. expo-secure-store fallback catch in loadKeychain catches the first require error and tries another module, but doesn't re-throw the original if both fail.
n/a — no interactive UI elements
Code fences in README.md have language labels (typescript, bash)

AES-GCM encryption/decryption lacks inline comments explaining why 12-byte IV is used (NIST recommendation for GCM mode). The key derivation/storage strategy isn't documented. The singleton pattern in WebSecureStorageAdapter isn't explained. No comments on security tradeoffs of storing the encryption key in IndexedDB.

No validation of data returned from external sources. keychain.getGenericPassword() result is used without checking its shape — assumes it has a .password property. The expo-secure-store wrapper assumes getItemAsync returns a string. IndexedDB getRequest.result is used without type checking.

trackedKeys from JSON.parse(result.password) is not validated per-item. If the stored JSON is corrupted or contains non-string entries, the wipe() method will iterate invalid data. No schema validation on the parsed array.
n/a — no iframe content
n/a — no CSP headers to set (module-level code)
n/a — no resolveRequest pattern

cachedAdapter singleton could get out of sync with platform state. If resetSecureStorageAdapter() is called but a reference to the old adapter is held, operations on the old adapter could conflict with the new one. Minor issue.

openDB() is called on every setItem, getItem, and removeItem — each call opens a new IDBDatabase connection. The database connection should be cached/reused. getOrCreateEncryptionKey() also opens DB and does a transaction on every encrypt/decrypt call.
Names are generally clear. Minor: keyNameForKey is a bit redundant; sanitizeKey would be clearer. loadKeychain does more than load — it also sets up fallbacks.
n/a — new module, no existing behavior to preserve
n/a — no balance display
keychain: any in ReactNativeSecureStorageAdapter is an unsafe type. getRequest.result is untyped in the web adapter. The expo-secure-store shim object is untyped. No type guards on external data.

Uses SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED which is a valid expo-secure-store option, but doesn't verify the enum exists at runtime. If the expo-secure-store version doesn't export WHEN_UNLOCKED, it would be undefined and silently fail.
n/a — no passkey operations in this module
SecureStorageAdapter interface is properly implemented by both adapters. Minor: the expo-secure-store shim doesn't fully implement the keychain API surface (resetGenericPassword throws).
n/a — no fetch/XMLHttpRequest interceptors
n/a — no raw HTML files

RN adapter wipe() only removes tracked keys. If keys were stored by a previous version that didn't track them, or if the tracked_keys entry is corrupted/deleted, those orphaned keychain entries survive the wipe. Not a complete keychain wipe.

wipe() iterates all tracked keys, but relies on the tracked keys list being complete and accurate. If setItem was called but setTrackedKeys failed, the key exists in keychain but not in the tracked list — it survives wipe.
Module never uses localStorage — web adapter uses IndexedDB with AES-GCM encryption, RN adapter uses platform keychain.
